subject: AWS Private Offer — term tagging, early-activation exception request
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@medicor.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-18T16:05:00Z
Subject: AWS Private Offer — term tagging, early-activation exception request

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I attached a one-pager that lays out the two common private-offer term structures we typically propose (1-year, 3-year) and what changes from a buyer-approval perspective when we co-sell through AWS. High level:

- 1-year: faster procurement, standard PO signing window, typically buyer approves at procurement + IT security.
- 3-year: better unit economics, often requires CFO/pricing approval and longer legal review.

You mentioned a hard requirement from procurement: Medicor needs the environment to be activated for pilot use prior to final PO signature in order to meet clinical timelines. We can support an "early activation" path but it usually requires an explicit activation exception (contract clause), a short-term credit or holdback, and SOC2 evidence in advance.

Attached: Redwood_PO_Term_Options.pdf (term comparison). Can you send the procurement checklist and any list of required evidence so our legal/ops teams can scope the exception?

Next steps I propose:
1) You send procurement evidence list and approximate approval timeline (days).
2) We align on early-activation terms (credit amount, holdback length).
3) Legal drafts an exception clause for review.

If it helps, Vivek will outline pricing levers we can apply to offset the operational risk.

—Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@medicor.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@medicor.com>, procurement@medicor.com
Date: 2028-09-18T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — term tagging, early-activation exception request

Kimberly —

Thanks for the summary and the term sheet. Quick answers: procurement expects a PO to be issued within 6 weeks for pilots, but the clinical team needs systems up in 2 weeks. That's why we asked about activation before final signature.

Evidence we need (minimum):
- SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months)
- Data residency confirmation (AWS region us-east-1)
- High-level network diagram + encryption-at-rest detail
- Copy of standard SLA and incident response contacts

On the credit/holdback: procurement will accept up to a 15% activation credit pending PO, but any credit must be reversible if we don't get a signed PO within the agreed window.

I attached a spreadsheet with our internal procurement fields so you can see the gating items.

—Sarah
Sr. Procurement Manager, Medicor Health
Attachment: Medicor_Evidence_Request.xlsx
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@medicor.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-18T20:03:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — term tagging, early-activation exception request

Sarah / Kimberly —

We can do the early activation with a simple set of commercial guardrails:
- Activation credit = 12% of the first 3 months' committed spend, applied as a billing credit.
- Activation window = up to 30 days of live usage before PO signature. If the PO is not signed within 30 days, the credit turns into an invoice and is payable in 30 days.
- Evidence gating: provide SOC2 summary + region confirmation before activation. Full report to follow within 7 business days.

On pricing: for a 1-year PO the list price shown in the term options is our baseline. If Medicor signs a 3-year PO we can introduce a step-down discount schedule (year 2 and 3). If procurement needs faster activation we recommend a 1-year with activation credit (lowest friction).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize the numbers.

—Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@medicor.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-19T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — term tagging, early-activation exception request

Sarah / team —

Legal here. We can draft an "Activation Exception" addendum that contains:
1) Explicit activation start date and scope (pilot cluster, limited users).
2) Credit mechanics and reversal conditions (as Vivek outlined).
3) Evidence acceptance criteria (SOC2 summary required up-front, full report within 7 business days).
4) Liability cap alignment (we will keep standard liability but recommend a 1.5x revenue cap for pilots).
5) Term-tagging language so that the AWS private-offer record indicates the purchase term (1yr/3yr) and whether activation exception was granted. This is important for AWS co-sell reconciliation and for SKU/discount mapping.

Operational asks: which Medicor entity will sign the PO (legal entity name + billing address)? Also confirm the required signer (Procurement vs CFO). We will circulate a redlineable addendum.

—Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-19T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — term tagging, early-activation exception request

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the procurement fields. To keep momentum:

1) We'll provision the pilot in us-east-1 within 48 hours after you confirm the signer entity.
2) We will require the SOC2 summary before activation; full report to follow within 7 business days.
3) Commercial: activation credit = 12% (as above), activation window 30 days.
4) Next: I asked Aditya to prepare a short addendum that tags the private-offer in AWS with the agreed term and flags the activation exception.

If you confirm the signer and the timeline by EOD tomorrow we'll send the DocuSign envelope for the addendum and the PO once procurement completes their fields.

Thanks — looking forward to getting your clinical team ramped.

Best,
